description: We are Team WildMinds. Our project is an interactive, statistically rigorous Earth system trend detector designed for students, researchers, and the scientifically curious public. We turn decades of raw NASA Earth observation data into proven, understandable climate evidence.
summary:
Earth Watch is an interactive rainfall and flood trend monitoring system designed to help users understand changing rainfall patterns and identify areas that may face increased flood-related risks.

Our project analyzes NASA satellite-based Earth observation data across five major river regions. It processes rainfall observations, examines historical trends, and classifies each monitored river region as Getting Wetter, Getting Drier, or No Clear Trend.

Through an interactive Streamlit dashboard, users can explore rainfall trends using visual charts, compare different river regions, view monitoring locations on an interactive map, and replay historical rainfall patterns over time. The platform also provides downloadable datasets for further analysis.

Earth Watch aims to make satellite-based environmental information easier to understand and more accessible. By highlighting changes in rainfall patterns, it helps users explore potential flood risks and better understand how Earth's water systems are changing.
details:
Earth Watch is a satellite-based rainfall and flood trend monitoring dashboard developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

The project focuses on identifying changes in rainfall patterns across five major river regions. It uses NASA Earth observation data to analyze rainfall over time and identify whether monitored regions are experiencing increasing rainfall, decreasing rainfall, or no significant trend.

The application is built using Python and Streamlit, with interactive visualizations powered by Plotly. It provides users with an overview of monitored rivers, individual river analysis, historical rainfall charts, an interactive geographical map, and downloadable data in CSV format.

One of its main features is the ability to classify rainfall trends into three categories: Getting Wetter, Getting Drier, and No Clear Trend. Users can also explore historical changes through an interactive timeline replay.

Earth Watch aims to make satellite-based environmental information easier to understand and explore. By highlighting rainfall trends in important river regions, the project helps users investigate changing water patterns and potential flood-related concerns.

The project combines data analysis, visualization, and an accessible interface to turn complex Earth observation information into understandable insights.
